# Introduction

Aim 1: To determine whether crickets are losing fluid from tissue   
Aim 2: To determine whether crickets are mobilizing lipid stores  

There are 5 treatment groups:

1. Control crickets 0 h of desiccation
2. 3 h of desiccation
3. 6 h of desiccation
4. 18 h of desiccation
5. 18 h of desiccation, then 6 h with water, no food (rehydration)
6. 18 h of desiccation, then 6 h with water **and** food (fed)

Treatment 6 was added because there is a strong effect of rehydration that is also explained by starvation. 

# Setup
```{r}
#| include: false
source("setup.R")
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

## Load data

**Note: Variable labels are not exactly the same as the other datasets but are equivalent.**

* Desiccation time: Time spent desiccating. Rehydrated crickets were desiccated for 18 hours
* Start mass: Mass (mg) at the start of the experiment before desiccation
* Whole animal wet mass: Mass (mg) after the end of the experiment. For control crickets (Time 0), end mass is start mass. For rehydrated crickets, mass is the same as post-desiccation mass.
* Rehydrated transfer mass: Mass (mg) of rehydrated crickets after 18 hours of desiccation.
* Tissue wet mass: Mass (mg) of wet tissue after blotting of haemolymph
* Tissue dry mass: Mass (mg) of dried tissue
* Haemolymph percentage: Percent (%) of whole animal wet mass that is haemolymph

```{r}
# Load mass data
tissue_data <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/Tissue water content/TissueWaterData.xlsx", sheet = "mass") %>%
  mutate(Desiccation_time = ifelse(Time == 24, 18, Time),
         Time_treatment = factor(Time_treatment, levels = c("0", "3", "6","18", "24_fed", "24_starved")),
         Time_plot = ifelse(Time_treatment == "24_fed", 25, Time),
         Start_mass = Start.Cricket - Start.Container,
         Whole_animal_wet_mass = case_when(Time == 0 ~ Start_mass,
                              .default = Beadmill.Cricket - Beadmill),
         Rehydrated_transfer_mass = ifelse(Time == 24, Transfer.Cricket - Transfer.Container, NA),
         Tissue_wet_mass = Beadmill.NoHaemolymph - Beadmill,
         Tissue_dry_mass = Beadmill.DryCricket - Beadmill,
         Percent_change = case_when(Time == 0 ~ NA,
                                    Time == 24 ~ 100 - (Rehydrated_transfer_mass / Start_mass) * 100,
                                    .default = 100 - (Whole_animal_wet_mass / Start_mass) * 100),
         Total_water_content = ((Start_mass - Tissue_dry_mass) / Start_mass) * 100,
         # Water lost during desiccation (%)
         Relative_water_loss = (Percent_change /  Total_water_content) * 100,
         # Calculate water loss rates
         Mass_change_rate = ifelse(Time == 0, NA, Percent_change / Desiccation_time) # %/h
  )
         
# Calculate water content in mg. Adds up to Body_water
tissue_data <- tissue_data %>% 
  mutate(
    # Total amount of water in body
    Body_water = Start_mass - Tissue_dry_mass,
    # Water lost during desiccation
    Lost_water = Start_mass - Whole_animal_wet_mass,
    # Water in tissue post-desiccation
    Tissue_water = Tissue_wet_mass - Tissue_dry_mass,
    # Haemolymph post-desiccation
    Haem_volume = Whole_animal_wet_mass - Tissue_wet_mass)
         
# Calculate proportion relative to total amount of body water
tissue_data <- tissue_data %>% 
  mutate(
    # Water lost during desiccation
    Lost_prop = ((Lost_water / Body_water) * 100),
    # Water in tissue post-desiccation
    Tissue_prop =  ((Tissue_water / Body_water) * 100),
    # Haemolymph post-desiccation
    Haem_prop =  ((Haem_volume / Body_water) * 100))

# Standardise tissue and haemolymph changes relative to controls
baseline <- tissue_data %>% 
  group_by(Sex) %>% 
  filter(Time == 0) %>% 
  summarise(mean_tissue = mean(Tissue_prop),
            mean_haem = mean(Haem_prop)) %>% 
  data.frame(row.names = c("F", "M"))

tissue_data <- tissue_data %>% 
  mutate(rel_tissue = ifelse(Sex == "Female", Tissue_prop / baseline["F","mean_tissue"],
                             Tissue_prop / baseline["M","mean_tissue"]),
         rel_haem = ifelse(Sex == "Female", Haem_prop / baseline["F","mean_haem"],
                             Haem_prop / baseline["M","mean_haem"]),
         rel_loss = (Body_water - Lost_water) / Body_water,
         diff_tissue = ifelse(Sex == "Female", Tissue_prop - baseline["F","mean_tissue"],
                             Tissue_prop - baseline["M","mean_tissue"]),
         diff_haem = ifelse(Sex == "Female", Haem_prop - baseline["F","mean_haem"],
                             Haem_prop - baseline["M","mean_haem"]))
```

## Rehydrated crickets

Calculate relative mass change during recovery to compare with other datasets.

```{r}
rehydration_tissue <- tissue_data %>% 
  filter(Time == 24) %>% 
  mutate(Percent_change = 100 - (Rehydrated_transfer_mass / Start_mass) * 100,
         Percent_change_recovery = (Whole_animal_wet_mass / Start_mass) * 100) %>% 
  select(Cricket_ID, Sex, Time_treatment, Percent_change, Percent_change_recovery) %>% 
  mutate(Start_Percent = 100,
         Percent_change = 100 - Percent_change) %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("Percent"), names_to = "Timepoint", values_to = "Change") %>% 
  mutate(Experiment = "Tissue",
    Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Start_Percent", "Percent_change", "Percent_change_recovery"))) 

save(tissue_data, rehydration_tissue, file = "data/Desiccation 2025/tissue.Rdata")

ggplot(rehydration_tissue, aes(Timepoint, Change, group = Cricket_ID, colour = Time_treatment)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.3) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  ylab("Relative mass change (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 120, 5), limits = c(70, 120), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point", labels = c("Pre-desiccation", "Post-desiccation", "Post-recovery")) +
  facet_grid(~Sex) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Changes in wet mass

```{r}
tissue_data %>% 
  mutate(Rehydrated_transfer_mass = ifelse(is.na(Rehydrated_transfer_mass), Start_mass, Rehydrated_transfer_mass)) %>% 
  select(Cricket_ID, Sex, Time_treatment,Start_mass, Whole_animal_wet_mass, Rehydrated_transfer_mass) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = matches(c("Start_mass", "Whole_animal_wet_mass", "Rehydrated_transfer_mass")), names_to = "Timepoint", values_to = "Mass") %>% 
  mutate(Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Start_mass", "Rehydrated_transfer_mass", "Whole_animal_wet_mass"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Timepoint, Mass, colour = Sex, group = Cricket_ID)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~Sex, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, 100), limits = c(70, 1000), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point", labels = c("Pre-desiccation", "Post-desiccation", "Post-recovery")) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```


# Are crickets losing haemolymph?

Measured gravimetrically. Indicating preferential loss or replenishment of extracellular fluid.

```{r}
mean_vol <- tissue_data %>% 
  group_by(Time_treatment, Sex, Time_plot) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Haem_volume),
            se = sd(Haem_volume) / sqrt(n()),
            cv = (sd(Haem_volume) / mean) * 100)
knitr::kable(mean_vol, digits = 3)

mean_vol_starved <- filter(mean_vol, Time_treatment != "24_fed")
mean_vol_fed <- filter(mean_vol, Time_treatment %in% c("18", "24_fed"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Haemolymph volume (mg) of female (orange) and male (blue) crickets after desiccation (hours). Error bars are standard error about the mean."
p_volume <- ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data = tissue_data, aes(Time_plot, Haem_volume, shape = Sex, colour = Sex), position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0), alpha = 0.6) +
     # line for starved crickets
  geom_line(data = mean_vol_starved, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex, linetype = "Starved")) +
   # Line for fed crickets
  geom_line(data = mean_vol_fed, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex, linetype = "Fed")) +
  geom_point(data = mean_vol, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex), 
             size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  geom_errorbar(data = mean_vol, aes(Time_plot, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se,
                                     colour = Sex), width = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = "Recovery", values = c("Fed" = 2, "Starved" = 1), labels = c("Food and water", "Water only")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Haemolymph volume (mg)", limits = c(0, 210), expand = c(0,0), breaks = seq(0, 250, 10)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time (h)", breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 18, 24), labels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "18 h + \n6 h recovery"), limits = c(-0.3, 25.3)) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_volume
```

## Stats: Haem volume

 * No interaction between time and sex. The interaction is dropped from the model.  
 * No differences between sexes. Sex is dropped from the model.
 * Crickets decrease haemolymph volume after 6 hours then recover volume.
 * No change within 3 hours.
 * No effect of feeding during recovery.
 
```{r}
hv_mod <- lm(Haem_volume ~ Start_mass + Time_treatment, tissue_data) 

anova(hv_mod)

pairs(emmeans(hv_mod, ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey") %>%
  broom::tidy() %>% 
  arrange(.$adj.p.value)
```

# Are crickets losing tissue water content?

Or are they preferentially losing water from their extracellular spaces instead.

Crickets are losing whole body wet mass during desiccation and their tissue wet mass. Their haemolymph mass is decreasing then increasing. Their dry mass was lower than the other treatments, so proportionally, they have lost more water from their tissue after drying in the oven, giving higher tissue water content.

```{r}
mean_tissue <- tissue_data %>% 
  group_by(Time_treatment, Sex, Time_plot) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Tissue_water),
            se = sd(Tissue_water) / sqrt(n()),
            cv = (sd(Tissue_water) / mean) * 100)
knitr::kable(mean_tissue, digits = 3)

mean_tissue_starved <- filter(mean_tissue, Time_treatment != "24_fed")
mean_tissue_fed <- filter(mean_tissue, Time_treatment %in% c("18", "24_fed"))
```

```{r}
p_water <- ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data = tissue_data, aes(Time_plot, Tissue_water, shape = Sex, colour = Sex), position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0, jitter.width = 0.1, dodge = 1.5), alpha = 0.6, stroke = NA) +
   # line for starved crickets
  geom_line(data = mean_tissue_starved, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex, linetype = "Starved"), linewidth = 0.5) +
   # Line for fed crickets
  geom_line(data = mean_tissue_fed, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex, linetype = "Fed"), linewidth = 0.5) +  
  geom_point(data = mean_tissue, aes(Time_plot, mean, colour = Sex),
             size = 2, shape = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = mean_tissue, aes(Time_plot, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se,
                                     colour = Sex), width = 1, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
  scale_linetype_manual(name = "Recovery", values = c("Fed" = 2, "Starved" = 1), labels = c("Food and water", "Water only")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Tissue water content (%)", limits = c(100, 450), expand = c(0,0), breaks = seq(0, 500, 50)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time (h)", breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 18, 24), labels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "18 h + \n6 h recovery")) 

p_water

ggsave(p_water, dpi = 300, width = ppt_width, units = "mm", height = ppt_height, filename = "data/Desiccation 2025/figures/tissue_water.png")
```

## Stats: Tissue water content

 * Strong sex differences: Females have more tissue mass than males. 
 * Proportion of water in tissue mass increases after rehydration. Losing tissue? Rather than over rehydrating.
 * No change within 3-6 hours.
 * Consistent effect of starvation:
     * Fed crickets were the same as the other time points.
     * Starved crickets had lighter dry mass, so has proportionally more water.
 
```{r}
tissue_mod <- lm((Tissue_water/Whole_animal_wet_mass) ~ Time_treatment * Sex, tissue_data) 

anova(tissue_mod)

pairs(emmeans(tissue_mod, ~ Time_treatment * Sex), adjust = "Tukey", by = "Sex") %>%
  broom::tidy() %>% 
  filter(adj.p.value <= 0.05)
```

### Relative change

No effect of sex
```{r}
anova(lm(rel_tissue ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data))

pairs(emmeans(lm(rel_tissue ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data), ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey") 

anova(lm(rel_haem ~ Time_treatment + Sex, tissue_data))

pairs(emmeans(lm(rel_haem ~ Time_treatment + Sex, tissue_data), ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey") 
```

### Difference

No effect of sex
```{r}
anova(lm(diff_tissue ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data))
anova(lm(diff_haem ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data))

pairs(emmeans(lm(diff_tissue ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data), ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey") 
pairs(emmeans(lm(diff_haem ~ Time_treatment, tissue_data), ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey")
```

# Are crickets using their lipid stores?

Load data
```{r}
#| warning: false
library(cellranger)

# Join sample mass with metadata
lipid_data <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/Tissue water content/TissueWaterData.xlsx", sheet = "lipid_sample_mass") %>% 
  left_join(., tissue_data, by = "Cricket_ID")

# Define the locations of the necessary files
lipid_plate_map <- "data/desiccation 2025/tissue water content/lipid_plate_map.xlsx"
lipid_spec_folder <- "data/desiccation 2025/tissue water content/spec_folder/lipid/"

# Get sample IDs for filtering data
list_sampleID_lipid <- list(lipid_data$Label)

# Load plate metadata
list_map_lipid <- lipid_plate_map %>% 
  # Get sheet names
  excel_sheets() %>%
  # Use sheet names to name the list
  set_names() %>% 
  # Import each sheet into a list
  map(read_excel, 
      path = lipid_plate_map, range = "A1:L8", col_names = paste(1:12))

# Get list names for housekeeping
list_names_lipid <- names(list_map_lipid)

# Load absorbance data. Every file in the folder should be the an xlsx file.
list_spec_lipid <- list.files(lipid_spec_folder, full.names = TRUE) %>% 
  # Import each file into a list
  map(read_excel, range = "B2:M9", col_names = paste(1:12), col_types = "numeric") %>% 
  # Use file names to name the list
  setNames(list_names_lipid)
```

```{r}
# Functions
# 1. load plate
f_plate <- function(platemap, spec){ 
  # Create data frame of absorbances and metadata 
  plate <- data.frame(grid = paste0(rep(LETTERS[1:8], 12), sort(rep(1:12, 8))),
                      well = 1:96,
                      Label = as.character(unlist(platemap)),
                      absorbance = as.numeric(unlist(spec))) %>%
    # Remove empty wells
    drop_na(Label)
  return(plate)
}
# Quality control function to identify deviant wells. Defaults to 10%
bad_well <- function(plate, deviance = 10){
  plate %>% 
    # Calculate median absorbance
    group_by(Label) %>% 
    mutate(median_abs = median(absorbance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>% 
    # Identify deviant wells within the tolerance range
    mutate(bad_well = ifelse(absorbance <= median_abs * (1 + (deviance/100))  & absorbance >= median_abs * (1 - (deviance/100)), "OK", "Remove")) %>% 
    # Remove surplus columns
    select(-median_abs) 
}
# 2. Correct for blank
f_correction <- function(plate){ 
  plate %>% 
    group_by(Label) %>% 
    # Calculate mean absorbance of the replicates
    summarise(mean_absorbance = mean(absorbance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    # Subtract the mean of the blank from the mean of the samples/
    mutate(corrected_abs = mean_absorbance - mean_absorbance[Label == "0"])
}
# 3. Fit standard curve
f_standard_curve <- function(plate, sampleID){

  standard_curve_model <- plate %>% 
    # Subset only the standards
    filter(!Label %in% sampleID) %>% 
    # Fit the linear model
    lm(corrected_abs ~ as.numeric(Label), .)
  
  # Extract the Coefficient of Determination
  r2 <- round(summary(standard_curve_model)$r.squared, 3) * 100 
  # Extract the slope and intercept
  slope <- standard_curve_model$coefficients[2] 
  intercept <- standard_curve_model$coefficients[1] 
  
  return(list(r2, slope, intercept, standard_curve_model))
}
# 4. Plot standard curve
standard_curve_fig <- function(corrected_plate, list_names, list_sampleID, standard_curve){
  # Plot of standards
  plot(corrected_abs ~ as.numeric(Label), corrected_plate[!corrected_plate$Label %in% list_sampleID,], 
       xlab = "Concentration",
       ylab = "Absorbance")
  # Fitted line
  abline(pluck(standard_curve, 4))
  # Plate ID and title
  title(paste0(list_names, " R2 = ", pluck(standard_curve, 1), "%"))
  # Equation of line
  text(y = max(corrected_plate$corrected_abs,na.rm = TRUE), 
       x = 0, 
       paste0("Absorbance = ", round(pluck(standard_curve, 2), 2), " x Concentration + ", round(pluck(standard_curve, 3), 2)),
       adj = c(0, 1))
}
# 5. Calculate well concentration
f_samples <- function(plate, standard_curve, sampleID){
  plate %>% 
    # Keep only samples
    filter(Label %in% c(sampleID)) %>% 
    # Calculate well concentration 
    mutate(well_conc = (corrected_abs - pluck(standard_curve, 3)) / pluck(standard_curve, 2))
}
# 6. Plot well concentration
well_conc_fig <- function(assay, list_names){
  # Plot of well concentrations
   barplot(well_conc ~ Label, assay, 
     xlab = "Sample",
     ylab = "Concentration",
     ylim = c(0, max(assay$well_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.2)) 
  # Plate ID and title
  title(list_names)
}
```

```{r}
spike_meta <- data.frame(plate = c("plate1", "plate2", "plate3", "plate4", "plate4", "plate5", "plate5", "plate6", "plate7", "plate7", "plate8", "plate8"),
  standard_conc = c(0.972, 0.972, 0.972, 0.972, 1, 0.972, 1, NA, 0.975, 0.972, 4.5, 4.5), 
                         vol_added = c(rep(75, 10), 20, 20), 
                         total_volume = 150,
                         spiked_ID = c("spike1", "spike2", "spike3", "spike4","spike4.chloroform","spike5", "spike5.chloroform", NA, "spike.old", "spike7", "spike8", "spike.buffer"),
                         unspiked_ID = c("55", "3", "66", "23", "23", "77", "77", NA, "50.repeat","50.repeat", "92", "buffer")) %>% 
  group_split(plate)

# Function of equation defined above
spike_recovery_fun <- function(assay, spike_metadata) {

spike_recovery <- ((assay[assay$Label %in% spike_metadata$spiked_ID,]$well_conc - assay[assay$Label  %in% spike_metadata$unspiked_ID,]$well_conc) / ((spike_metadata$standard_conc * spike_metadata$vol_added) / spike_metadata$total_volume)) * 100

spike_metadata$spike_recovery <- if(length(spike_recovery) != 0) {
  spike_recovery
  } else {NA}
  return(spike_metadata)
}

# Return spike recovery (%) as list in order of plates
spike_recovery <- map2(list_well_conc_lipid, spike_meta, spike_recovery_fun) %>% list_rbind()
spike_recovery
```

> All spike recoveries are low. Using standard A gave extra high recoveries. Reason unclear.

* 1 mL C:M volume
* Lipid content is relative to tissue dry mass, not whole animal

```{r}
vanillin_drymass <- function(assay){

assay$sampled_tissue_mg <- (assay$Sample_mass / (1 * 2/3)) * 0.15
assay$mg_lipid_per_mg_tissue <- assay$well_conc / (assay$sampled_tissue_mg / 0.15)
assay$total_lipid <- assay$mg_lipid_per_mg_tissue * assay$Tissue_dry_mass
assay$lipid_percent <- (assay$total_lipid / assay$Tissue_dry_mass) * 100

# standardised values to 100 mg tissue dry mass 
assay$standardised_total <- assay$mg_lipid_per_mg_tissue * 80
assay$standardised_percent <- (assay$standardised_total / 80) * 100

return(assay)
}
```

## Stats: Total lipids

```{r}
full_l_mod <- lmer(total_lipid ~ Start_mass * Time_treatment * Sex + (1|Plate), data = lipid_data, REML = FALSE)

anova(full_l_mod)
# Three way interaction is not significant

total_l_mod <- update(full_l_mod, .~. - Start_mass:Time_treatment:Sex)

best_l_mod <- step(full_l_mod)
print(best_l_mod)
# Model selection drops three way interaction
# Random term is not significant but keeps term

anova(total_l_mod)

pairs(emmeans(total_l_mod, ~ Time_treatment * Sex), adjust = "Tukey", by = "Sex") %>%
  broom::tidy() |> 
  filter(adj.p.value <= 0.05)
```

## Stats: Lipid per dry mass

 * No interaction.
 * There is a strong sex difference between males and females. Females have more lipid
 * There is an overall time effect with 24h starved crickets being different to the control.
 * There is a sex difference during recovery but this is not significant:
     * Fed females do not change their lipid content but starved females do. Likely a starvation effect
     * Starved males do not change their lipid content, but fed males do. Since their total lipids don't change, perhaps they are not assimilating lipids, but spending more.
 
```{r}
lipid_mod <- lmer(mg_lipid_per_mg_tissue ~ Time_treatment + Sex + (1|Plate), lipid_data) 
anova(lipid_mod)

pairs(emmeans(lipid_mod, ~ Time_treatment), adjust = "Tukey") %>%
  broom::tidy() 

emmeans(lipid_mod, ~ Time_treatment) %>% 
  contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1) 
```

**Mixed effects model: Plate as a random effect**  

 * No interaction
 * No main effect of time - only between 0 and 24 (starved)

# Are crickets using carbohydrates?

Quality control: Plate 6 has degraded samples compared to the other plates because the box was kept at -20C for a week. Keep only three of the points and sample 96.

```{r}
# Join sample mass with metadata
carb_data <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/Tissue water content/TissueWaterData.xlsx", sheet = "carb_sample_mass") %>% 
  left_join(., tissue_data, by = "Cricket_ID") %>%

# Define the locations of the necessary files
carb_plate_map <- "data/desiccation 2025/tissue water content/carb_plate_map.xlsx"
carb_spec_folder <- "data/desiccation 2025/tissue water content/spec_folder/carb/"

# Get sample IDs for filtering data

# Load plate metadata

  # Get sheet names
  excel_sheets() %>%
  # Use sheet names to name the list
  set_names() %>% 
  # Import each sheet into a list
  map(read_excel, 
      path = carb_plate_map, range = "A1:L8", col_names = paste(1:12))

# Get list names for housekeeping

  # Import each file into a list
  map(read_excel, range = "B2:M9", col_names = paste(1:12), col_types = "numeric") %>% 
  # Use file names to name the list
  setNames(list_names_carb)
```

```{r}
                         standard_conc = 0.5,

# Function of equation defined above
spike_recovery_fun <- function(assay, spike_metadata) {

spike_recovery <- ((assay[assay$Label %in% spike_metadata$spiked_ID,]$well_conc - assay[assay$Label  %in% spike_metadata$unspiked_ID,]$well_conc/2) / spike_metadata$standard_conc) * 100

spike_metadata$spike_recovery <- if(length(spike_recovery) != 0) {
  spike_recovery
  } else {NA}
  return(spike_metadata)
}

# Return spike recovery (%) as list in order of plates
spike_recovery <- map2(list_well_conc_carb, spike_meta, spike_recovery_fun) %>% list_rbind()
spike_recovery
```

* 0.25 mL of water added to pellet
* 0.5 mL supernatant extracted from initial digestion
* 1 mL of KOH added to dry tissue

```{r}
anthrone <- function(assay){
  assay$pellet_carb <- assay$well_conc * 0.25
  assay$sample_carb <- (assay$pellet_carb / 0.5) * 1
  assay$mg_carb_per_mg_tissue <- assay$sample_carb / assay$Sample_mass
  assay$total_carb <- assay$mg_carb_per_mg_tissue * assay$Tissue_dry_mass 
  assay$carb_percent <- (assay$total_carb / assay$Tissue_dry_mass) * 100
  
  return(assay)
}

carb_content <- map(list_well_conc_carb, anthrone) %>% list_rbind(names_to = "Plate")
carb_data <- left_join(carb_data, carb_content, by = c("Label", "Sample_mass", "Tissue_dry_mass")) %>% 
  filter(Include_for_carb == 1)
```

# Conclusions

1. Are crickets losing haemolymph?

Yes, after 6 hours but both sexes restore the proportion of haemolymph after rehydration. This trend is also found in absolute haemolymph mass (mg). 

2. Are crickets losing tissue water? 

Even though crickets are losing wet mass throughout desiccation, they are maintaining the proportion of water in their tissue. Water is maintained even after using tissue (dry mass) at 18 hours.

Tissue wet mass increases during rehydration for starved crickets but this is an increase in fluid, not in tissue so tissue dry mass is unchanged. This indicates rehydration observed as an increase in % tissue water.

In fed crickets, water content does not differ to other time points, despite an increase in tissue dry mass (feed). Crickets are rehydrating but not over hydrating.

Thus, crickets are not losing tissue water and are increasing hydration state during recovery.

3. Are crickets using tissue? 

Crickets do not appear to be using tissue at any time during desiccation. 

Starved crickets are losing mass. This is likely an effect of starvation than desiccation. Fed crickets are gaining dry mass. Much of this mass is likely food in the gut.

4. Are crickets using their lipid stores?

Overall, crickets are using lipids after 24 hours, but this effect is not conserved within sex. This pattern is likely because of starvation.

This lack of a trend could be explained by crickets metabolising tissue, as indicated by their tissue dry mass. Thus, proportional amount of lipid in the tissue is the same because the overall amount of tissue is lowered. 

Male crickets are not using lipid stores if they are starved, but are using lipid stores if they are fed. Could they be more active or less conservative if feed is available? 

5. Are crickets using their protein stores?

Crickets are not using their protein stores. There is no difference between the amount of protein at 0 h and 18 h. Their total protein increases if they are fed, likely from the feed itself.

6. Are crickets using their carbohydrate stores?

No, they are not.

> Crickets are able to tolerate and recover from desiccation. These tissue-level trends are more pronounced for females than males. Cricket are not losing dry mass during desiccation. Thus, there is limited support for using fat stores to aid recovery of water during desiccation.

> There is support for starved crickets to be using their macromolecules during recovery. Their dry mass decreases post-recovery mass with a higher water content and with a lower lipid content. They appear to be preferntially burning lipid over protein.
